newsitem.title: USA: Industrial output gains modestly in July.
newsitem.headline: Industrial output gains modestly in July.

text.p: Industrial production rose a slim 0.2 percent last month, the Federal Reserve said Thursday, as a drop in light truck manufacturing partly offset gains in aircraft and high-technology output.
The figure was in line with economists' forecasts, and followed a 0.3 percent gain in June. Analysts said the report was another sign of steady growth with low inflation.

The capacity use rate, which measures how near to production limits businesses are operating, slipped to 83.1 percent last month from a revised 83.3 percent in June. The Fed had previously estimated the June rate at 83.5 percent.

"With capacity utilization down to 83.1 percent, we are even further away from the inflationary pressure point than we were before this release. This will not do anything to change the Federal Reserve's view," said Lou Crandall, chief economist at R.H. Wrightson and Associates, an economic research firm in New York.

Fed policy-makers are to meet Tuesday to consider their next move on interest rates. They last raised short-term rates on March 25, the first increase in more than two years, in a bid to ward off inflation. The central bankers have held rates steady since.

Leading the overall rise in industrial output last month was a 0.9 percent rise in aerospace products, a 2.6 percent rise in computer and office equipment and a 2.7 percent rise in semiconductor production, the Fed said.

Total motor vehicle assemblies fell in July to a rate of 11 million a year from 11.7 million in June. Despite a slight rise in the July assembly rate for autos, output of light trucks, which includes vans and sport utility vehicles, plunged almost 15 percent, the Fed said.
Excluding motor vehicles and parts, overall industrial output rose 0.3 percent last month after a 0.2 percent increase in June, it said.
Output of durable goods rose 0.3 percent last month. Non-durable goods production fell 0.2 percent, reflecting declines in clothing, chemical product, paper product and fuel output, it said.

Broken down by sector, the Fed said factory output rose 0.1 percent in July after rising 0.3 percent a month earlier. Production by mining industries, which includes oil drilling, fell 0.3 percent in July and in June.
Electric and gas utilities, reacting to more seasonal summer temperatures after cool May and a moderate early June, boosted output by 1.5 percent in July, the Fed said.
